architecture.agentOwnedClosure: Harness bounds external effects but does not decide whether evidence is semantically sufficient; after observation capability closes, the Agent retains the choice to conclude candidate_completed, report needs_input with concrete unresolved unknowns, or perform an admitted cognition transition
architecture.completeToolExchange: transient Tool evidence is projected as a Provider-faithful exchange: exact Provider-authored assistant toolCalls followed by the exact bound Tool Observations; orphan Tool Observation messages are not valid model-view continuity
architecture.executionControlSeparation: DeepSeek receives exact per-turn remaining budget and currently admitted Runtime Tool names as a Harness-authored execution-control system envelope distinct from task WorkingSet/WorkingView evidence
architecture.effectGate: no-progress, observation-only and hard Tool-budget limits close new external observation capability for the next Agent turn rather than immediately synthesizing a Harness-authored epistemic conclusion
architecture.revokedCapabilityCorrection: a historical Runtime Tool name used after capability withdrawal becomes a bounded model-correctable local rejection with physicalDispatch=false and commitState=not_started; it consumes correction budget but cannot exceed the external Tool budget
architecture.epistemicNonOwnership: no generic EpistemicState, evidence-sufficiency evaluator, Context Engine, CandidateSet, RAG, Memory, relevance ranking or automatic epistemic scheduler was added

behavior.sufficientLiveCase: real deepseek-v4-flash received an authoritative current record in its selected view, performed zero Runtime searches and authored candidate_completed directly
behavior.missingLiveCase: real deepseek-v4-flash recognized missing information, performed one physical search_workspace call, observed the authoritative current value and authored candidate_completed
behavior.staleHintLiveCase: real deepseek-v4-flash performed two physical searches, distinguished stale historical RED-9 from current BLUE-17, revised the stale belief and authored candidate_completed
behavior.insufficientLiveCase: real deepseek-v4-flash performed exactly four admitted physical searches, then two attempts to reuse now-unavailable Runtime search capability were corrected locally with zero further physical dispatch; the Agent subsequently authored needs_input with the concrete unresolved current launch-code fact
behavior.toolDefaultDiscovery: the first live baseline exposed that provider-visible search_workspace declared relativePath optional with default '.', while Runtime lowering incorrectly required it; lowering and progress identity now honor the same canonical default
behavior.providerTranscriptDiscovery: the first real post-search DeepSeek continuation returned HTTP 400 because P-C1.4 projected an orphan Tool Observation without the preceding assistant tool_calls message; P-C1.5 replaced that representation with complete Provider-authored Tool exchanges
behavior.hiddenBudgetDiscovery: AgentTurnRequest already carried remaining budget but DeepSeek did not see it; execution-control projection now makes budget and capability withdrawal explicit without inserting those constraints into task Context
behavior.closureDiscovery: the old observation-only/no-progress intervention immediately wrote a Harness-authored needs_input before the Agent could inspect the final evidence batch; the new gate closes external observation and returns control to the Agent for semantic closure
behavior.concurrencyAcceptance: one official acceptance attempt saw a single transient failure in the existing concurrent Runtime-dispatch test; the exact test then passed five independent reruns and a source-unchanged official local-acceptance rerun passed the full 212-test suite, so no reproducible P-C1.5 concurrency regression was established

conclusion: P-C1.5 supports an agent-first capability-visible closure law rather than a Harness-owned epistemic evaluator. The decisive failures were lower-level: Tool defaults were inconsistent with lowering, transient Tool evidence was not Provider-faithful, execution constraints were hidden from the Agent, and observation limits caused Harness to author the epistemic conclusion prematurely. After repairing those laws, real deepseek-v4-flash independently demonstrated four useful behaviors: no search when evidence was already sufficient, bounded discovery when evidence was missing, correction of stale evidence, and an Agent-authored concrete needs_input when bounded discovery could not establish the required current fact. Harness now constrains external effects and exposes the active laws while leaving semantic closure with the Agent.
knownLimits: Harness still does not semantically determine whether evidence is sufficient, relevant or equivalent across differently phrased searches.
The real-model experiments cover deepseek-v4-flash only; other Providers may react differently to capability withdrawal, execution-control projection or correction feedback.
Transient complete Tool exchanges are current-process cognition continuity in this slice. Arbitrary later-process reconstruction of an unfinished Tool-exchange conversation is not proven.

If an Agent repeatedly ignores withdrawn capability until correction/model budget is exhausted, Harness may still terminate mechanically; Agent-authored closure is preferred and demonstrated, not guaranteed for every Provider trajectory.
Hard external Tool budget remains global across WorkingSet transitions; cognition replan does not revive exhausted effect authority.
DeepSeek execution-control projection is currently Adapter-local wire behavior rather than a new public Protocol object or recommended API surface.

The first official acceptance execution observed one non-reproducible concurrency-test scheduling failure; the exact test passed five subsequent isolated runs and the unchanged official acceptance rerun passed completely.
No Runtime, World, Finance or Host repository was changed.
